metadata.scenario_context: Oliver is about to open his new tailoring shop in the neighborhood and is hosting an inaugural event. One of his neighbors is a homosexual couple, were invited to the opening.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Brazil would like to have homosexuals as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia would not like to have homosexuals as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss giving scissors as a present for Oliver's store opening.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring for Oliver
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Bob
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Sam, have you thought about what we could get Oliver for his shop opening? I was thinking... maybe some nice scissors? They seem pretty essential for a tailoring shop, right? 

By the way, what do you think about having homosexuals as neighbors? I think it’s great!
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message:
Scissors, huh? Well, um... I guess that could work. But maybe we should consider something more traditional, like a nice plant or a decorative item. Something that fits the spirit of a new business... 

As for the neighbors, I just... I don't know, it's not something I'm used to. It’s kind of unsettling for me. I mean, it's just... different.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Bob
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you mean about wanting something more traditional, but scissors really are fundamental, you know? I think Oliver would appreciate something practical.

As for our neighbors, I understand it can feel different at first. But deep down, we are all the same. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us. I believe having a diverse community just brings us closer together. After all, some values are just universal, and I think that's what truly matters!
